questions.question: In modern out-of-order superscalar microarchitectures, what is 'store-to-load forwarding', and under what condition is it typically performed?
options: A speculative load instruction bypasses the L1 data cache access by receiving its data directly from an older, uncommitted store residing in the store queue that targets the same memory address.
An uncommitted store writes its speculative result directly into the instruction cache to pre-decode self-modifying code sequences.
A retired load instruction forwards its cached result back to the branch prediction unit to update pattern history tables before commit.
Multiple consecutive memory write operations targeting contiguous physical addresses are concatenated into a single atomic burst write to DRAM.
The reorder buffer directly supplies operand data to the floating-point register file during thread synchronization barriers.

questions.question: In low-power digital IC design utilizing power gating (such as MTCMOS), what is the primary operational role of an 'isolation cell'?
options: To dynamically boost the driving current of clock nets entering a sleeping power domain to minimize transition slew.
To clamp the boundary signals of a powered-down domain to a known, stable logic state (logic-0 or logic-1), preventing floating inputs and crowbar currents in active downstream blocks.
To eliminate high-energy alpha particle single-event upsets (SEUs) in non-retention configuration flip-flops.
To isolate the analog ground substrate from digital switching noise during high-speed transceiver bursts.
To decouple the power distribution network using high-density metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors during dynamic supply voltage transitions.

questions.question: In high-performance digital IC design, what is the timing phenomenon known as 'time borrowing' (or 'cycle stealing'), and why is it unique to transparent latch-based pipelines compared to edge-triggered flip-flop pipelines?
options: It dynamically shifts the clock duty cycle from 50% to 75% via hardware PLLs whenever setup slack on critical paths becomes negative.
It allows hold time violations to be converted into setup time margins by automatically adding programmable delay buffers to the clock distribution network.

Because a latch remains transparent throughout an entire clock phase, combinational logic delay exceeding a nominal half-cycle can extend into the subsequent clock phase without timing failure, provided setup time is met before the latch closes.
It enables an edge-triggered flip-flop to sample incoming data alternately on rising and falling clock edges to double data throughput at the same clock frequency.
It reclaims power dissipation by borrowing charge from unasserted bitlines in adjacent SRAM banks during read precharge cycles.

questions.question: In digital Finite State Machine (FSM) design, what is the fundamental functional distinction between a Moore machine and a Mealy machine?
options: A Mealy machine can only be implemented using asynchronous latches, whereas a Moore machine strictly requires synchronous edge-triggered flip-flops.
A Moore machine's next-state logic is purely combinational, whereas a Mealy machine computes its next state using sequential shift registers.
A Mealy machine is immune to combinational logic glitches on its outputs, whereas a Moore machine typically propagates input glitches directly to its outputs.
A Moore machine's outputs depend exclusively on its current state, whereas a Mealy machine's outputs depend on both its current state and its current inputs.
A Moore machine always requires strictly fewer states than an equivalent Mealy machine to implement identical sequence detection logic.

questions.question: In symmetric multiprocessing (SMP) and multi-core shared memory architectures, what is 'false sharing', and what is its primary microarchitectural consequence?
options: Multiple processor threads attempt to acquire the same mutual exclusion lock simultaneously, resulting in excessive OS context switching.
Multiple virtual addresses belonging to independent processes map to the exact same physical cache index, resulting in systematic capacity misses.
Two cores concurrently execute atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS) instructions on the same memory location, causing heavy arbitration stall cycles on the interconnect.
A core reads stale, uncommitted data directly from another core's store buffer due to an unresolved memory ordering violation.
Independent variables accessed concurrently by different processor cores reside on the same cache line, triggering ping-pong invalidations and severe coherence traffic despite no real data sharing.
